answer: Treat the agent graph itself as the cost surface. A new identity remains a leaf until it is accepted as a vertex with edges to three non-overlapping witness clusters. Each cluster must have aged like a juniper stand: long, unshared custody rather than a subnet spun up overnight. Influence travels only along those edges, so a farm parked on one side of a canyon of shared infrastructure cannot reach the others without buying independent operators. Cloned accounts add isolated leaves, never new bridges, and therefore cannot concentrate vote or emission weight.
